Generative AI Development & RAG Solutions | SASTRAVA SASTRAVA 
 Home 
 
 About 
 
 Services 
 
 Portfolio 
 
 Contact 
 
 Insights 
 
 SASTRAVA · Consulting · Technology · Growth 
 
 Generative AI and retrieval-augmented generation 
 
 Explore whether a language model or AI assistant fits your users and information needs. SASTRAVA can help scope a bounded prototype, connect selected reference material, and plan evaluation, privacy, and human review. 
 
 Connect answers to selected information 
 
 A retrieval-augmented generation system retrieves relevant material from an approved source collection and provides it to a language model when responding. Access, freshness, source quality, and evaluation all affect usefulness. 
 
 Information and user workflow discovery 
 
 Source selection and access requirements 
 
 A bounded prototype with review criteria 
 
 Plan for limitations and oversight 
 
 Generative AI may return inaccurate or incomplete answers. Testing, clear source references, access controls, user feedback, human review, and fallback paths should be considered before wider use. 
 
 Privacy and security review for selected data 
 
 Evaluation for representative questions 
 
 Operational and human-review plan 
 
 How we work 
 
 Choose a user problem and approved source material. 
 
 Define prototype scope, access controls, and evaluation. 
 
 Review results and decide whether a wider rollout is justified. 
 
 Common questions 
 What is retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)? RAG connects a language model to selected reference material so its responses can use relevant information retrieved for a question. When should a business use a custom AI assistant? An assistant may help when users need a conversational way to find information or complete a bounded workflow, with access controls and evaluation suited to the data involved. Does generative AI always return correct answers? No. Generative AI can produce inaccurate responses. Testing, clear source material, suitable guardrails, human review, and monitoring are important for production use.

pages.content:
Business, Technology & Digital Growth Insights | SASTRAVA SASTRAVA 
 Home 
 
 About 
 
 Services 
 
 Portfolio 
 
 Contact 
 
 Insights 
 
 SASTRAVA · Consulting · Technology · Growth 
 
 Insights for better business and technology decisions 
 
 These practical guides help founders and business teams think through AI automation, cybersecurity, local marketing, and early-stage business decisions. Each guide explains a useful starting point, trade-offs, and next steps without promising specific results. 
 
 Practical guidance, grounded in real questions 
 
 SASTRAVA’s insights focus on decisions that founders, business teams, and learners face when adopting technology or planning growth. Useful topics include choosing an automation use case, preparing for a security review, building a digital product, and measuring marketing activity. 
 
 Business consulting, startup planning, and innovation 
 
 AI, automation, software delivery, and cybersecurity 
 
 Brand strategy, SEO, digital marketing, and digital learning 
 
 Editorial standards 
 
 Advice should explain its assumptions, distinguish general information from a project-specific recommendation, and avoid promises about rankings, security, or commercial outcomes. New guides are published when they are ready for review. 
 
 Use clear sources and explain technical terms 
 
 Keep recommendations proportionate to the evidence 
 
 Contact SASTRAVA to discuss a specific organizational context 
 
 5 minute guide 
 
 How to choose a useful first AI automation 
 
 Start with a recurring workflow and a measurable problem. Decide whether AI is needed only after you understand the task, data, and risk. 
 
 Start with the work, not the tool 
 
 List the steps people repeat, where delays occur, and what a mistake would cost. A suitable first project is usually a bounded task with a clear owner and a result that can be checked. Examples include classifying incoming requests, drafting a first response for human review, or consolidating information from approved sources. 
 
 Check whether AI is the right fit 
 
 If the task follows stable rules, a form, integration, or ordinary automation may be simpler and easier to maintain. Consider AI when the work involves language, variable inputs, or patterns that are difficult to express as fixed rules. Identify what data the system may use and whether it contains personal, confidential, or regulated information. 
 
 Run a bounded pilot 
 
 Define a small test set, expected output, human review steps, and a safe fallback before connecting a system to live work. Track completion time, correction rate, and failure types. Keep a person responsible for decisions that affect customers, money, access, or safety. Expand only when the pilot is useful, secure, and supportable. 
 
 Explore AI and automation consulting 
 
 6 minute guide 
 
 What to include in a small business website security review 
 
 A practical review checks the site, its hosting and integrations, how data is handled, and whether the team can respond to findings. 
 
 Agree the scope and permission first 
 
 List the domains, applications, APIs, cloud accounts, and third-party services that are in scope. Confirm who owns each system, which tests are authorized, and when they may run. A written scope reduces disruption and prevents tests from reaching customer or supplier systems that were not approved. 
 
 Review common control areas 
 
 Check account access and multi-factor authentication, software and dependency updates, secure configuration, backups, logging, and how secrets are stored. For forms and APIs, review validation, rate limits, access control, data retention, and exposure of personal information. The depth of testing should match the system and agreed authorization. 
 
 Turn findings into a fix plan 
 
 For each issue, record affected assets, evidence, likely impact, and a practical remediation owner. Prioritize based on exposure and business impact rather than a score alone. Patch or change configuration within the agreed scope, then retest the specific finding. A review describes what was examined; it cannot prove that a system is completely secure. 
 
 Explore security audit services 
 
 5 minute guide 
 
 A practical local growth plan: search, brand and paid media 
 
 Connect local search visibility and brand communication to a clear offer, useful landing page, and conversion measurement before increasing spend. 
 
 Make the offer and service area clear 
 
 Use consistent business details and explain who the service is for, what problem it addresses, and where the business serves customers. Keep the website, business profile, and social profiles aligned. Do not create location pages that repeat the same copy with only a city name changed. 
 
 Build a useful landing page 
 
 Answer the questions a prospective customer needs before contacting you: scope, process, deliverables, relevant experience, and a direct next step. Add proof only when it is accurate and approved for publication. Use descriptive links to connect the page to related services and contact options. 
 
 Measure before scaling 
 
 Set up call, form, and messaging conversion measurement and define what counts as a qualified inquiry. Organic search can compound over time; paid search or social can test an offer and audience more quickly but spend should follow budget approval. Review lead quality and cost alongside traffic before expanding campaigns. 
 
 Explore brand and performance marketing 
 
 5 minute guide 
 
 A first business discovery plan for early-stage founders 
 
 A focused discovery plan helps founders test a customer problem, clarify the offer, and decide what evidence they need before building. 
 
 Describe the customer problem 
 
 Write down who experiences the problem, what they do today, and why the current option is inadequate. Speak with people who fit the intended customer group and ask about recent behavior rather than asking whether they like an idea. Record themes and counterexamples so early assumptions do not become facts. 
 
 Clarify the offer and constraints 
 
 Explain the proposed outcome in plain language, who pays, and how delivery could work. List the people, skills, time, costs, permissions, and technology the idea depends on. Identify the smallest test that can reduce an important uncertainty without overbuilding. 
 
 Choose the next decision 
 
 Set a review point and decide in advance what evidence would justify continuing, changing direction, or stopping. A business model and roadmap are working hypotheses, not guarantees of funding or growth. Use what you learn to focus the next experiment and revisit assumptions as customer evidence changes.

 Search engine optimization and local search services 
 
 Improve how people discover and understand your site with technical review, query research, useful content, and consistent local business information. SEO work is prioritized against your audience, competition, and implementation capacity; rankings cannot be guaranteed. 
 
 Fix crawlability and page foundations 
 
 Start with indexable, useful pages, consistent canonicals, descriptive titles, clear headings, fast mobile experiences, and internal links that help visitors move through relevant content. 
 
 Technical crawl and indexability review 
 
 Page titles, descriptions, headings, and structured data 
 
 Mobile experience and internal-link improvements 
 
 Create content for real search intent 
 
 Query research can reveal what customers are trying to solve. Build focused service pages and genuinely useful answers rather than repeating keywords or making unsupported claims. 
 
 Keyword and audience-intent research 
 
 Service and editorial content planning 
 
 Local business information consistency 
 
 How we work 
 
 Review the site, audience, and current search opportunities. 
 
 Prioritize technical fixes and useful content. 
 
 Measure discovery and conversion signals and refine over time. 
 
 Common questions 
 How long before we see SEO results? Timing varies with the site’s current condition, competition, content, budget, and implementation pace. We agree measures and review progress over time; no fixed timeline can be promised. Do you guarantee rankings? No. Search rankings and business results depend on competition, the offer, budget, audience, and execution. We agree a plan, report progress, and refine work using available evidence. What is your SEO approach? We follow Google guidelines using white-hat techniques: quality content, technical optimization, authority building, and user experience. Can you improve existing rankings? Yes, we analyze current rankings, identify gaps, and develop strategies to improve positions for underperforming keywords. What is the difference between SEO, AEO, and GEO? SEO helps people discover useful pages in search. Answer engine optimization (AEO) makes clear answers easy to find and understand. Generative engine optimization (GEO) helps generative search systems interpret trustworthy, useful information. None can guarantee inclusion or a particular ranking.
